sign list.notes:
Ideo. in 𓊃𓀀𓏤 s (si) 'man'. Ideo. or det. 'I', 'me' in 𓀀 i, 𓅱𓀀 wi, 𓏌𓎡 ink, 𓎡𓅱𓀀 kwi. Det. man's relationships or occupations, exx. 𓅭𓏤𓀀 sꜢ 'son'; 𓋴𓍋𓂋smr 'courtier'; 𓎛𓅨𓂋𓅱𓅨𓀀 ḥwrw 'wretch'; 𓁹𓂋𓂋 irr 'doer'; also personal names, ex. 𓋹𓈖𓐍𓅱𓀀 ꜥnḫw 'ꜥAnkhu'. In personal names, 𓀀𓏥 is abbrev. for 𓂋𓎛𓅱𓀀𓏥 rḥw 'men', ex. 𓀀𓏥𓋹𓈖𓐍 Rḥw-ꜥnḫ 'Reḥuꜥonkh'.
Seated man and woman with plural strokes: Det. people and their occupations, exx. 𓂋𓍿𓀀𓁐𓏥 rmṯ 'people'; 𓌙𓅓𓅱𓀀𓁐𓏥 ꜥꜢmw 'Asiatics'; 𓂸𓏏𓂋𓅱𓂭𓂭𓀀𓁐𓏥 mtrw 'witnesses'.
Det. eat, exx. 𓃹𓈖𓅓𓀁 wnm 'eat'; 𓎛𓈎𓂋𓀁 ḥqr 'hungry'; drink, ex. 𓋴𓅨𓂋𓇋𓈗𓀁 sw(r)i 'drink'; speak, exx. 𓋴𓆓𓂧𓀁 sḏd 'relate'; 𓎼𓂋𓀁 gr 'be silent'; think, ex. 𓎡𓄿𓀁 kꜢi 'devise'; feel, ex. 𓌻𓂋𓀁 mri 'love'.
Det. in 𓈞𓊃𓀂 ḥmsi 'sit'. Replaced in hieratic by 𓀔 A 17 or 𓀕 A 17* or even by 𓁓 B 4.
Det. supplicate, ex. 𓇼𓄿𓀃 dwꜢ 'adore'; hide, exx. 𓋴𓂧𓎼𓄿𓀃𓂻 sdgꜢ 'be hidden'; 𓇋𓏠𓈖𓀃 imn 'hide'.
Det. hide, ex. 𓇋𓏠𓈖𓀄𓏛 imn 'hide'.

sign list.description: man receiving purification (in M.E. usually replaced by 𓃂 D 60)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in 𓀆 var. Pyr. 𓅱𓂝𓃂 wꜥb 'pure', 'clean'.

sign list.description: man sinking to ground from fatigue
sign list.notes: Det. weary, weak, exx. 𓅨𓂋𓂧𓀉 wrd 'tire'; 𓃀𓂧𓈙𓀉 bdš 'faint'; 𓎼𓈖𓈖𓀉 gnn 'be soft'.
Det. in 𓉔𓈖𓏌𓅱𓀊 hnw 'jubilation'.

sign list.description: man steadying basket (𓎺 W 10) on his head
sign list.notes: Det. in 𓄿𓍿𓊪𓀋 abbrev. 𓀋𓂝 Ꜣṯp 'load'; 𓆑𓄿𓀋 abbrev. 𓀋𓂝 fꜢi 'carry'; 𓂓𓏏𓀋 abbrev. 𓀋 kꜢt 'work'.
Det. in 𓋴𓐪𓂧𓏌𓀌 sqdw 'sail'.

sign list.description: man holding the aba scepter 𓌂 S 42 and crook 𓋿 S 39 (O.K.)
sign list.notes: O.K. ideo. or det in 𓀍 var. 𓐍𓈖𓅓𓋴𓀍 ḫnms 'friend'. Later replaced by 𓀙 A 21.
Ideo. or det. in 𓀎𓏪 var. 𓅓𓈙𓂝𓀎 mšꜥ 'army'. Det. in 𓏠𓈖𓆑𓇋𓇋𓏏𓀎𓏪 mnfyt 'soldiers'

sign list.description: man with arms tied behind his back
sign list.notes: Det. enemy, exx. 𓋴𓃀𓇋𓌙𓀏 sbi 'rebel'; 𓐍𓏏𓆑𓀏 ḫfty 'enemy'.

sign list.description: man with blood streaming from his head.
sign list.notes: Det. die, ex. 𓅓𓏏𓀐 mwt 'die'; enemy, ex. 𓐍𓏏𓆑𓀐 ḫfty 'enemy'.

sign list.description: as A 14 but blood interpreted as an axe
sign list.notes: Use as A 14.
Ideo. or det. in 𓐍𓂋𓀒 ḫr ‘fall’ and derivatives. Abbrev. 𓀒𓅱 for 𓐍𓂋𓅱𓀒 ḫrw ‘fallen (i.e. conquered) enemy’; also 𓀒𓏏 for 𓋴𓐍𓂋𓏏𓀒 sḫrt ‘overthrow’ (infinitive).
Det. in 𓎡𓋴𓀓 ksi ‘bow down’.

sign list.description: child sitting (on lap) with hand to mouth
sign list.notes: Det. young, exx. 𓂋𓈖𓊪𓆳𓀔 rnpi ‘be young’; 𓈙𓂋𓇋𓀔 šri ‘child’; 𓈖nmḥ ‘orphan’. Abbrev. for ẖrd ‘child’. Phon. nni in Nni-nsw ‘Heracleopolis’.

sign list.description: child in sitting posture, arms hanging down
sign list.notes: Adapted from hieratic, where it replaces # A 3, ex. ḥmsi ‘sit’, or 2 A 17, ex. msw ‘children’.

sign list.description: child with crown of Lower Egypt S 3
sign list.notes: Det. child-king, exx. inp 'crown prince', 'royal child'; wḏḥ 'weaned princeling'.

sign list.description: bent man leaning on stick (clearly distinquishable from A 21 in hieratic, not always so in hieroglyphic).
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. old, in iꜢw 'old'; smsw 'eldest'; great in wr 'great one', 'chief'. Det. old, also in tni 'old'; lean, exx. rhn 'lean; twꜢ 'support oneself'. Phon. or phon. det. ik (from a rare iꜢk be aged) in iky 'miner', 'hewer of stone'. In M.K. hieratic is used in ḥwi, ḥii 'strike'.

sign list.description: man leaning on forked stick, less senile than A 19
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in smsw (śmśw) 'eldest', especially in sꜢ.f smsw 'his eldest son', cf. Pyr. zꜢ.k śmśw, and in the title smsw hyt 'elder of the portal'

sign list.description:
man holding stick in one hand and hand-
kerchief in the other (always disting from A 19 in hieratic)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in sr (śr) 'official', 'noble'. Det. magnate, exx. šnyt 'courtiers'; smr 'courtier', 'friend' (of the king). Also det. in ḫnms 'friend', here replacing an older sign + A 11; in ẖnti 'statue' replacing 8A 22. In hieroglyphic 7 is often hard to distinguish from 5 A 19 (in the word wr 'chief') and from 6 A 20.

sign list.description: statue of a man with stick in aba-sceptre S 42
sign list.notes: Det. in ẖnt(y) 'statue' and in twt 'statue'. The form of the sign varies according to the nature of the statue to be depicted.

sign list.description: king with stick and club T 3
sign list.notes: Det. in ity 'sovereign'.

sign list.description: man striking, with left arm hanging behind back
sign list.notes: Rare ideo. used in ḥwi, ḥii 'strike'.  In papyri of Dyn. XII 'strike' is written  with a sign identical to  A 19.

sign list.description: man with one arm raised in invocation
sign list.notes: Det. call, exx. nis 'call', 'summon'; ḏwi 'call'. Abbrev. ꜥš in sḏm-ꜥš 'servant', lit. 'one who hears the call'. Det. in the vocative interjection i 'O'.

Det. high, in kꜢ(i) 'be high'.  Det. joy, exx. ḥꜥi 'rejoice'; swꜢš 'extol'; mourn, in ḥꜢi 'mourn'; also, for unknown reasons, in iꜢs 'bald'.
Det. in sḫd 'be upside down'.

sign list.notes: Det. turn away, ex. ꜥnw 'averted' (face).
Det. dance, ex ḫbi 'dance'; joy, ex. hy-hnw 'jubilate'.

sign list.description: man with stick and bundle or mat on shoulder
sign list.notes: Ideo. in m(i)niw 'herdsman'.  Det. wanderer, exx. rwi 'wander'; šm(Ꜣ)w 'wanderers', 'strangers'.
Det. in ḫwsi 'pound', 'build'.
Ideo. or det. in qd 'build'.

sign list.description: man kneading and straining into a vessel
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ꜥfty 'brewer'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: man holding necks of two emblematic animals with panther heads (Dyn. XII)

Use as last.

sign list.description: seated god (Note the slightly curved beard and straight wig)
sign list.notes: Det. god (replacing earlier  G 7), exx. Ptḥ 'Ptah'; Mnṯw '(the god) Mont'. Ideo. or det. 'I', 'me', in i, wi, ink when a god is speaking or, in Dyn. XII, the king.

sign list.description: king.  (Note uraeus on brow, straight beard, and coif)
sign list.notes: Det. king (common Dyn. XVIII), exx. nsw 'king'; ḥm 'majesty; nb 'the Lord" .  Ideo. or det. 'I', 'me' in i, wi, ink when the king is speaking.

sign list.description: the same but with flagellum S 45.

sign list.description: king wearing crown of Upper Egypt S 1
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in nsw (nzw, ni-śwt) 'king of Upper Egypt', 'king'. Det. Wsir 'Osiris'.

sign list.description: the same, but with flagellum S 45
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.description: king wearing crown of Lower Egypt
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in bity 'king of Lower Egypt'.

sign list.description: shepherd seated and wrapped in mantle, holding a stick with appendage.
sign list.notes: Ideo. in m(i)niw 'herdsman'. Ideo. or det. in sꜢw 'guard', 'protect'. Sometimes inaccurately for  A 48 in iry 'relating to'.
Ideo. or det. iry in 'relating to', 'belonging to'.
Det. foreigner, exx. ꜥꜢmw 'Asiatics'; ꜥiwntyw-styw 'Nubian bowmen'.

sign list.description: man of rank seated on chair
sign list.notes: Det. revered persons (M.K.; in Dyn. XVIII mainly replaced by  A 51 and  A 52), exx. snbw 'Sonbu', or personal name; smr(w) 'courtiers'. Ideo. or det. 'I', 'me' on M.K. coffins in i, wi, ink. Rarely ideo. like  A 51 šps (špś) 'noble'.
Ideo. in špsi (špśi)'be noble' and related words. After M.K., often det. revered persons. ex. imyw-ḥꜢt 'those of former times'.

sign list.description: noble squatting with flagellum S 45 (common in Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Det. revered persons, especially personal names, ex. PꜢ-ḥry 'Paheri', a man's name; sꜥḥ 'deceased noble'. Rarely also for  A 51 in šps 'noble'.
Det. mummy, ex. wi 'mummy'; statue, likeness, ex. twt 'statue'; form, shape, exx. ki 'form'; ḫprw 'forms', 'stages of growth'.
Det, dead, exx. m(i)ni 'death'; nb-ꜥnḫ 'sarcophagus', lit. 'lord-of-life'.

sign list.description: mummy lying on bed (replacing O.K. form with man on bed).
sign list.notes: Det., lie, ex. sḏr 'lie', 'spend all night'; death, exx. ḫpt 'deceased'; ẖꜢt 'corpse'.
Det. 'drive away' in sḥr 'drive away'.

Det. female, exx. st ‘woman’; ḥmt ‘woman’, ‘wife’; ntrt ‘goddess’; woman’s relationships, exx. sꜢt ‘daughter’; ẖꜢrt ‘widow’; her occupations, exx. ḥmt ‘female slave’; šmꜥyt ‘chantress’; her name, ex. Nfrt ‘Nofret’.  As suffix 1st pers. sing. ‘I’, ‘my’ (fem.) i has not been noted before Dyn XIX.
Det. pregnant, exx. iwr ‘conceive’; bkꜢ ‘be pregnant’.
Ideo. or det. in msi (mśi) ‘bear’, ‘give birth’ and the related words.

sign list.description: combination of sign for a squatting woman (cf. B 3) with F 31.
sign list.notes: Use as last. In one hieratic MS. substituted for A 3.
Det. ‘suckle’ in mnꜥt ‘nurse’, ‘foster-mother’.

sign list.description: woman seated on chair with child on lap
sign list.notes: Det. ‘nurse’ in rnn ‘nurse’, ‘rear’.

sign list.description: queen wearing diadem and carrying flower
sign list.notes: Det. of names of queens.

sign list.description: god with sun and uraeus on head
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Rꜥ (the sun god) Ra.

sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Rꜥ '(the sun god) Ra'.
Ideo. or det. in Ḏhwty 'Thoth'.

sign list.description: god with head of ram E 10
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in H̱nmw 'Khnum'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: god with head of dog E 15
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ꜥI͗npw 'Anubis'; also in Wp-wꜢwt 'Wepwawet'.

sign list.description: god with head of Seth animal E 20
sign list.notes: Ideo. in Stẖ (Śtš) 'Seth'.

sign list.description: ithyphallic god with feathers, uplifted arm and flagellum S 45
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Mnw 'Min'.
Ideo. or det. in Ḥt-ḥr 'Hathor'.
Ideo. or det. in MꜢꜥt 'Maat', the goddess of Truth.

sign list.description: god with arms supporting (the sky) and M 4 on head (often also without M 4)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in Ḥḥ ('one of the gods) Heh'.  Hence pron. ḥḥ in ḥḥ 'millions', 'many'.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Ideo. in tp 'head' and tpy 'chief', 'first'. Det. head, exx. ḏꜢḏꜢ 'head'; ḥꜢ 'back of head', whence prep. ḥꜢ 'behind' and mkḥꜢ 'neglect'; dhnt 'forehead', whence dhn 'promote', etc.; perhaps with notion throttle, in gwꜢwꜢ 'fetter', 'bind fast'. Possible possessed the value ḏꜢḏꜢ in some cases where there is no evidence to prove it. Of the two words for 'head' ḏꜢḏꜢ alone has survived into Coptic.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ḥr 'face' and derivatives. Hence the phon. ḥr, exx. ḥr 'prepare'; dḥr 'bitter', 'sour'.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Det. hair, exx. šny 'hair'; skm 'grey-haired'; skin, exx. iwn 'complexion', 'nature'; inm 'skin'; mourn, in iꜢkb 'mourn'; bald, empty, forlorn, exx. wš 'fall out (of hair)', whence abbrev. in gm wš 'found defective' (of damaged writing or pictures); ẖꜢrt 'widow'.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Ideo. in irt 'eye'. Hence phone ir, exx. iri 'make'; irtt 'milk'. Det see, in mꜢꜢ 'see', whence as phon. mꜢ in mꜢw 'lions'. Early det. in other words for see, look, and in connection with other notions involving the eye, exx. dgi 'look', šp 'blind'; rmi 'weep'; rs 'be wakeful'; later, especially in Dyn. XVIII, mainly replaced as det. by the more specific signs  D 5,  D 6,  D 7 and  D 9. From the end of Dyn. XVIII a masc. dual ...wy 'eyes' is occasionally found, but whether this points to the existence of a masc. word ir 'eye' is uncertain.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Det. actions or conditions of eye, exx. dgi 'look'; šp 'blind'; rs 'be wakeful'.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Sign for 1/8 hekat-measure of corn. Also doubled as det. for inḥ 'eye-brow(s)'. Det. or phon. det. in some words connected with smd (śmd) 'eye-brow' itself not found until Greek times.

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body

sign list.category_group: D, Parts of the human body
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in fnḏ, later fnd, 'nose'. Det. nose, ex. 'nose', 'nostril'; smell, exx. tpi 'sniff'; sn 'smell'; face, in ḫnt 'face'; joy, exx. rš(w) 'rejoice'; ḫntš 'take pleasure'; soft, kind, ex. sfn 'be mild'; also in bṯn 'be disobedient'; gfn 'rebuff'. From ḫnt 'face' (see above), phon. det. and (seldom before Dyn XIX) phon. ḫnt, exx. ḫnty 'in front of' (adj). Owing to similarity in hieratic  sometimes appears in hieroglyphic for Aa 32, ex. sty 'red (?) Nubian (?) pigment'; also for  U 31, ex. ḫni for ḫn(r)i 'restrain'; the hieratic has been often transcribed wrongly in modern books. Confusion of two different stems has contributed to the confusion of signs in words like ḫnrt, varr. ḫnt 'prison', 'harem', 'fortress', which are consequently hard to differentiate.

sign list.notes:

sign list.notes: Phon. wr, exx. wr 'great'; wrḥ 'anoint'.  A similar sign is det. in mnt 'swallow'.
Det. small, exx. nḏs (nḏś) 'small'; ḥns 'narrow'; bad, defective, exx. bin 'bad'; šw 'empty'; mr 'ill', 'diseased'; Ꜣq 'perish'.

Det. in O.K. gb 'the gb-goose'; hence semi-phon. gb in Gb, var. Gbb, '(the earth-god) Geb'. Det. in r, trp, names of kinds of geese; also in Ꜣpd 'bird', 'goose'.  This type may be employed in place of the more exact  G 39 in words containing sꜢ (zꜢ), except when the originals clearly mark the pintain.  It may be employed for the indeterminate birds serving as phon. det. in wfꜢ 'talk'; wsf 'be idle'; wdf 'delay'; and ḥtm 'perish'.  Lastly, it may be used for the generalized det. of birds and insects found in hieratic, exx. ṯnḥr  'hawk'; niw 'ostrich'; snḥmw 'locusts'.

Det. in st (zt, perhaps for zꜢt) 'pintail duck'. Hence phon. sꜢ (zꜢ), exx. sꜢ 'son'; sꜢw 'beam', 'plank'; ḥsꜢt 'the divine ḥsꜢt-cow'. This type may, if preferred, be employed in the place of  G 38 in the indefinite uses where the actual nature of the bird in question is unknown.

Ideo. in Pyr. pꜢ 'fly'.  Hence phon. pꜢ, exx. pꜢ 'the'; spꜢ 'centipede'.  In group-writing is used for p.  In Dyn. XII  is occasionally used for G 41.  In hieratic  is always replaced by  G 41, as also oaccasionally in hieroglyphic.

Det. in ḫni 'alight', 'halt'; hence phon. det. ḫn, ex. ḫn 'speech', 'sentence'.  For unknown reasons, phon. or phon. det. qmi in qmyt 'gum'; phon. det. sḥw in sḥwy 'collect'.  The combination  is used to show that  is the throw-stick  T 14, not the identically shaped warrior's club, served as det. in qmꜢ 'throw', whence qmꜢ 'create'; also in mtn , O.K. mṯn, 'nomad hunter', whence phon. det. ṯn, tn, exx. mṯn 'road'; ṯni, var. tni, 'distinguish'.  Before Dyn. XVIII  is sometimes used for  G 40 in hieroglyphic, as always in hieratic, where it often serves, like  G 38, as an indefinite det. for birds.
Ideo. in wšꜢ 'fatten'; also in ḏf(Ꜣ) 'provisions'.

For unknown reason, phon. w.
For , the hieroglyphic adaption of the hieratic abbreviated forn of  G 43, see Z 7.

sign list.description: two quail chicks G 43 as monogram
sign list.notes: Phon. ww, ex. pḥww 'end'.
Phon. wꜥ, ex. wꜥw 'soldier'.
Phon. mꜢw, ex. m mꜢwt 'anew'.
Ideo. in ṯꜢ 'nestling'. Hence phon. ṯꜢ, exx. ṯꜢy 'male'; ṯnṯꜢt 'baldachin'. In group-writing ( with single stroke) is used for ṯ.
Det. in sš (zš?) 'nest'.  Sometimes written with a single duckling.

sign list.description: ducks' heads protruding form a pool
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in sš (zš?) 'bird-pool', 'nest'.
In rḫty 'fuller', 'washerman'.
Det. in ḥꜢm 'catch fish'.
Det. in snm (śnm) 'feed' (trans. vb.).

sign list.description: human headed bird preceded by R 7 (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Ideo in bꜢ 'soul'.
Det. in wšn 'wring neck of (birds)', 'offer'. For unknown reason, phon. or phon. det. in snḏ, var. Pyr. śnḏ, later var. snd, 'fear' and derivatives.
In formula of offering as abbrev. of Ꜣpdw 'fowl'. det in wšn 'wring neck of (birds)', 'offer'. This type may be used for H1 H 2 in transcribing hieratic mꜢꜥ when the crest is absent.

Phon. det. mꜢꜥ, exx. mꜢꜥ 'temple' (of head), cf. mꜢꜥ 'real'. Also phon. or phon. det. wšm, exx. wšm 'ear (of corn)'; wšmw 'vessel (for beer)'. From Dyn. XII in place of H2 H 3 as phon. pq (pꜢq) in pqt 'fine linen'.
Phon. det. pꜢq (pq), ex. pꜢq 'pꜢq-cake'.
Phon. det. nr, ex. nrw 'terror'.  From Dyn. XVIII sportive writing in rmṯ 'people'.
Det. wing, ex. ḏnḥ, var. dnḥ, 'wing'; fly, exx. ꜥẖi 'fly'; pꜢ 'fly'.

Ideo. in šwi 'feather'. Hence phon. šw, ex. Šw '(the air-god) Shu'. Ideo. as substitute for H6 C 10, in mꜢꜥt 'truth'; in the adjective mꜢꜥ 'true' and related words H6 is not written, nor has it been found in M.E. hieratic in any words from this stem.
With one or two strokes at side in M.E. hieratic for words from the stem šw.
Phon. šꜢ in ŠꜢt '(the land) Shat'.

Det. in swḥt (śwḥt) 'egg'.  The hieratic contraction of  G 39 found in the inverted M.K method of expressing filiation appears in Dyn.XIX hieroglyphic as the egg ; that sign may be conventionally used in transcribing the instances in M.K. hieratic.  In pꜥt 'patricians', 'mankind'  is perhaps derived from an earlier sign for a clod of earth.
Det. in ḥntꜢsw 'lizard'; ꜥš(Ꜣ) 'lizard'. From the latter, phon. ꜥšꜢ in ꜥšꜢ 'many' and the related words.
Ideo. or det. in štyw 'turtle'.

Ideo. or det. crocodile, exx. msḥ (mzḥ) 'crocodile'; ḫnty 'crocodile'; however, for the god Sobek the sign  I 5* or  I 4 is perhaps invariably used. Det. greedy, in skn 'lust after'; ḥnt 'be greedy'; perhaps also in ꜥẖm 'voracious (?) spirit'; aggression in Ꜣd 'be aggressive', 'angry'. For obscure reason, phon. it in ity 'sovereign'.
Ideo or det. in Sbk (Śbk) '(the crocodile-god) Sobek'.
Det. in sꜢq (śꜢq) 'collect', 'gather together'.

sign list.description: archaic stone (?) image of a crocodile
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Sbk (Śbk) '(the crocodile-god) Sobek'.
Cf. ikm 'shield'. Hence (?) phon. km, exx. Kmt 'Eypt'; skm 'grey-haired'.
Det. in Ḥqt '(the frog-goddess) Heket.  From Dyn. XVIII of XIX sometimes as sportive ideo. for wḥm ꜥnḫ 'repeating life' as epithet after personal name.
Cf. the O.K. name of a man Ḥfnr, i.e. 'Tadpole'.  Hence phon. ḥfn in ḥfn 'one hundred thousand', plur. var. Dyn. XIX ḥfnw.

Ideo. perhaps in the name of the XIIth nome of Upper Egypt 𓈋𓆑𓊾𓈈Ḏw-ft ‘Mountain of the Horned Viper’, for which a rare var. with 𓆑𓏏ft occurs; cf. also demotic fy ‘viper’. Hence phon. f. 
For 𓊥 see P 9. For 𓋵 see S 30. For 𓍚 see U 35.

Cf. Pyr.𓆓𓏤 ḏ var. 𓆓𓏏𓆘ḏt 'cobra'. Hence phon. ḏ. Sometimes also, by false archaism, for 𓂧d.
For 𓇆 see M 14. For 𓌌 see T 5. For 𓎓 see V 21.

Phon. ḏd, ex. 𓎗𓅱𓆕𓏏𓏛wḏdt 'what had been commanded'.
For 𓌍 see T 6.

sign list.description: cobra (erect as on the forehead of the Pharaoh)
sign list.notes: Det. in iꜥrt 'uraeus'.  Det. goddesses, especially those to whom the appearance of a snake was attributed, exx. WꜢḏyt '(the goddess) Wadjet'; Nsrt (Nzrt) '(the goddess) Nesret'.

sign list.description: cobra I 12 on the basket V 30
sign list.notes: Det. goddess, exx. WꜢḏ(y)t 'Wadjet'; ntrt 'goddess'.  As an element in the royal title  see G 16.
Det. snake, exx ḥfꜢw 'serpent'; ḏdft 'snake'; possibly also det. worm, but it is doubtful if ḏdft ever had that usually attributed meaning.
Use as last.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Det in int 'the bulti-fish'.  Hence phon. in, exx. int 'valley'; inb 'wall'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Phon. det. bw in bwt 'abomination'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Det. in Ḥdw 'the buri-fish'.  Hence phon. ꜥd (ꜥḏ?) in the title ꜥḏ(?)-mr, var. ꜥd-mr, 'administrator (of a province)', probably lit. 'excavator of canal(s)'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ẖꜢt 'oxyrhynchus'.  Hence phon. ẖꜢ, exx. ẖꜢt 'corpse'; ẖꜢrt, var. ḫꜢrt, 'widow'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Phon. det. bs (bz) in bs, var. O.K. ibz, 'introduce', 'enter'.  A very similar fish is used as generic det. fish, ex. rmw 'fish'; fishy smell, ex. ḫnš 'stink'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in nšmt 'fish-scale'.

sign list.category_group: K, Fishes and parts of fishes
sign list.notes: Det. of špt 'be discontented'.
Ideo. in ḫprr 'dung-beetle'. Hence phon. ḫpr in ḫpr 'become' and derivatives.
Ideo in bit 'bee'; also in bit 'honey'.  Hence phon. bit in bit(y) 'king of Lower Egypt'.
Det. in ꜥff 'fly'.
Det. in snḥm (Pyr. znḥm) 'locust'.
Det. in spꜢ (Pyr. zpꜢ) 'centipede'.
For unknown reason, phon. ḫꜢ, in M.E. only in ḫꜢt, var. ḫꜢwt, 'table of offerings'.
Ideo. in Srqt '(the scorpion goddess) Serqet', full name in Pyr. Śrqt-ḥtw 'she who-relieves-the-wind-pipe'.

Det. tree, exx. nht 'sycamore-fig', 'tree', plur. often nhwt; mnw 'trees'; nbs 'Christ's thorn-tree', 'nebq-tree'; iꜢm, varr. Pyr. iꜢm, im(Ꜣ), unidentified tree.  From this last, phon. iꜢm, im--writings with  are best transcribed iꜢm--exx. iꜢmt 'charm', 'favor'; iꜢm(w) 'tent'.  The rather similar sign which serves as det. in mꜥr 'fortunate' may well depict a quite different object.

Det. plant, flower, exx. iꜢrw 'reeds'; ḥrrt 'flower'. From ḥni 'rush', phon. ḥn, exx. ḥnw 'vessel'; ḥnskt 'lock' (of hair). Det. in isi 'be light' (perhaps like isw reeds); hence phon. det. is, exx. isy, var. O.K. iz, 'tomb', 'chamber'; iswt 'old times'. From  'reed (see on M 17) rarely as sportive writing for i 'I', 'my'; hence also for as det. ex. s 'man'. From Dyn XVIII on sometimes as faulty transcription of hieratic  T 24 in iḥwty 'tenant farmer'.

Ideo. in ḫt 'wood', 'tree'; hence phon. ḫt, exx. ḫtyw 'terrace'; nḫt 'strong'.  Det. wood, ex. hbny 'ebony'; wooden objects, exx. wḫꜢ 'column'; qniw 'palanquin'.  Vertically in ḏꜥr, var. ḏꜥ, 'search out', lit. perhaps 'harpoon' (vb.); here it is probably corruption of an old sign.

sign list.description: palm-branch stripped of leaves and notched to serve as tally
sign list.notes: Det. in rnpi 'be young', 'vigorous'.  Hence rnp in rnpt 'year', with  ideographically as symbol; with similar sense ideo. in ḥsbt 'regnal year' and in snf (from śn.nw.f 'its second) 'last year'.  Possibly ideo. of time (if not phon. det.) also in tr 'time', 'season', where it usually appears in the form  M 5 or  M 6.  Elsewhere also  is an occasionaly substitute for  M 5,  M 6, or  M 7.

With sportive ideographic intention (palm-branch planted in ) in Pyr. tr, var. t(i), 'season'.  Hence  (see on M 4 for ) becomes in M.E. characteristic det. in tr 'season'.  However,  M 6 is a commoner substitute for , though  interchanges with  in some uses really belonging only to the latter, exx. pri 'battlefield'; TꜢ-mri 'Ta-meri', i.e. Egypt.

With sportive intention in Pyr. tr 'season'.  In M.E. det. in tr 'season'.  Hence phon. det. tr, ti, exx. tr 'pray'; ḥtr  'assess' (taxes); also phon. det. ri, exx. pri 
battlefield'; TꜢ-mri 'Ta-meri', i.e. Egypt.
With sportive ideographic intention in Pyr. rnpi 'be young', 'vigorous'.  Hence, in M.E., ideo. or det. in rnpi 'be young' and derivatives.

Ideo. in šꜢ 'lotus pool', 'meadow'.  Hence phon. šꜢ, exx. šꜢ 'appoint', 'command'; šꜢd 'dig'.  In group-writing  or  is used for š.  From Pyr. iꜢḫi 'be inundated', ideo. or semi-ideo. in Ꜣḫt 'inundation season'.
Ideo. or det. in sšn, var. Pyr. zššn, 'lotus'.
Det. in nḥbt 'lotus-bud'.
Ideo. or det. in wdn 'offer'.  In late Dyn. XVIII also erroneously in place of  F 46 as det. in w(Ꜣ)ḏbw 'shores'.

sign list.description: leaf, stalk and rhizome of lotus
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ḫꜢw nw sšn 'lotus plants'. Hence phon. ḫꜢ, exx. ḫꜢ 'thousand'; sḫꜢ 'remember'. In group-writing  or  is used for ḫ.

Ideo. in wꜢḏ 'papyrus column', cf. Pyr. wꜢḏ 'papyrus'. Hence phon. wꜢḏ in wꜢḏ 'be green' and derivatives. From M.K., phon. w(Ꜣ)ḏ as substitute for  V 24, exx. sw(Ꜣ)ḏ 'hand over', 'bequeath'; w(Ꜣ)ḏḥ, var. Pyr. wdḥ, 'pour out'.
Phon. wꜢḏ, w(Ꜣ)ḏ, exx. WꜢḏ-wr 'the sea', lit. 'the great green'; sw(Ꜣ)ḏ 'hand over', 'bequeath'.

sign list.description: clump of papyrus with buds bent down
sign list.notes: Det. papyrus and watery regions, exx. idḥw 'swamps' (of the Delta); ḏyt 'papyrus marsh'.  Phon. det. wꜢḫ in wꜢḫ(y) 'hall of the Inundation' from the Pyr. stem iꜢḫi, whence Ꜣḫ 'thicket' (of papyrus). Hence phon. Ꜣḫ (or ideo?) in Ꜣḫ-bit 'Chemmis' (a Delta place), possibly understood as 'Papyrus-thicket of the King of Lower Egypt'.  Det. in TꜢ-mḥw 'Lower Egypt', 'the Delta', whence mḥ-s 'the crown of Lower Egypt'.

Phon. ḥꜢ, exx. ḥꜢ 'would that!'; ḥꜢq 'capture'. In group-writing  or  is ḥ. As O.K. det. in TꜢ-mḥw 'the Delta' and related words  is often replaced in M.E. by  M 15, but exx. with  are still fairly common, exx. TꜢ-mḥw 'the Delta'; mḥ-s 'crown of Lower Egypt'.
Ideo. in i 'reeds'. Hence phon. i.
In ii 'come' and the related words.

sign list.description: heaped conical cakes between reed M 17 and sign like U 36
sign list.notes: Det. in ꜥꜢbt 'offering', 'pile of offerings' and the related verb.
Ideo. or det. in sḫt (śḫt) 'marshland', 'country' and its derivative sḫty 'peasant'.  Occasionally phon. sm (śm) like M 21, ex. sm 'occupation', 'pastime'.

sign list.description: like the last, but with a loop at the side
sign list.notes: Ideo. or semi-ideo. In sm, var. Pyr. śm 'herb', 'plant'. Hence phon. sm (śm), ex. sm 'succour'.

Cf. Pyr 𓈖𓐍𓃀𓏏𓇑nḫbt 'germination', 'shooting up'. Hence phon. 𓇑𓃀𓏏𓅐𓎟nḫb in 𓈖𓐍𓃀𓇑𓏏𓅐Nḫbt '(the vulture goddess) Nekhbet'.
For , two rushes with shoots, Cf. nnt 'rushes'. Hence  is phon. nn, exx. nn 'this'; nni 'be weary'.

sign list.description: plant regarded as typical of Upper Egypt (probably form of M 26, but without flowers)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in swt (śwt) 'the swt-plant'. Hence phon. sw (św), ex. swt 'but'. The word 'king of Upper Egypt' probably originally read ni-śwt 'he who belongs to the swt-plant', but before M.K. had become nsw (nzw); 'kingship' is perhaps to be read nsyt. Sometime  is inaccurately used for  M 24 or  M 26. In group-writing  stands for s.
With sportive pictoral intention (plant śwt growing from mouth r), phon. rśw in Pyr. rśwt 'South' and the related words. In M.E. 'South' is rsy.
Faulty writing either for words connected with rswt 'South', ex. rsyw 'southerners', or for words connected with Šmꜥw 'Upper Egypt', ex. Šmꜥ 'Upper Egyptian corn'.

sign list.description: sedge (?) growing from a sign for land resembing N 17
sign list.notes: Probably as a flowering specimen of  M 23, ideo in Šmꜥw 'Upper Egypt', the reading of which is given by šmꜥ 'make music'. Hence phon. šmꜥ in šmꜥyt 'chantress', 'singer'.
In Šmꜥ(w) 'Upper Egypt'.  Also phon. šmꜥ in šmꜥyt 'chantress', 'singer'.
In the title wr mḏw Šmꜥ(w) 'greatest of the tens of Upper Egypt'.

sign list.description: pods from some sweet smelling tree
sign list.notes: Cf. nḏm 'nḏm-tree'.  Hence semi-phon. nḏm in nḏm 'sweet' and the related words.  The tree or wood ssnḏm is possibly a later deformation of an O.K. word śśḏ or ššḏm.
Ideo. or det. in bnr 'sweet' and derivatives.

sign list.description: stylized rhizome of a lotus (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Det. in rd 'grow'.
Use as last.  A similar sign sometimes in hieratic erroneously borrowed from rd 'grow' in r(w)d 'be strong'.

sign list.description: grains of corn (also written vertically or grouped)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in it 'barley', 'corn' and its varieties it Mḥ 'Lower Egyptian corn' and it Šmꜥ 'Upper Egyptian corn'.  Det. corn, ex. Npri (the grain-god) Nepri'.
Ideo. or det. in bdt, var. bty, 'emmer'.
Det. in ꜥḥꜥw 'heaps'; also in wbn 'overflow'.

sign list.description: bundle of flax stems showing the bolls (sometimes misinerpreted)
sign list.notes: Phon. ḏr, exx. ḏr 'since'; nḏri 'hold fast'.  Det. in dmꜢ 'bind together'.

sign list.description: bundle of flax stems (O.K. form of M 36)
sign list.notes: Phon. ḏr like  M 36.

sign list.description: bundle of flax (O.K.; specialized variant of M 37)
sign list.notes: Det. in O.K. mḥꜥ (?), var. Dyn. XII mꜥḥ (?), mḥ (?), 'flax' and in dmꜢ 'bind together'.
Det. vegetable offerings, ex. rnpt 'vegetables', 'fruit'.
Cf. isw 'reeds'.  Hence phon. is (iz), exx. is (iz) 'tomb'; iswt 'crew'.

sign list.description: log of wood stripped of its branches (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Det. wood, exx. ꜥš 'cedar' (properly 'pine' or 'fir'); wꜥn 'juniper (?)'; mr(w) 'meru-wood'.

Phon. wn, exx. wnḏw 'short-horned cattle'; ḥwn 'be young'; wnm 'eat'.  Not distinguished from  Z 11 in the earliest hieratic, and replaced by the latter sign in M.K. hieratic, as also regularly in later hieroglyphic.
Det. vine in i(Ꜣ)r(r)t 'vine'; various notions connected with the vine, exx. irp 'wine'; kꜢmy 'gardener'; fruit generally, exx. dꜢb 'figs'; išd 'išd-fruit'.
Det. in srt 'thorn'. Possibly it is the same sign, if not a mere triangle, which serves as ideo. or det. in spd (śpd) 'sharp' and the related words.

Ideo. or det. in pt 'sky'. det. sky, exx. Nwt '(the sky goddess) Nut'; ḥrt 'heaven', lit. 'the distant one'; high, in ꜥḫi 'hang'. In I͗n-ḥrt '(the god) Onuris'  is a later interpretation, since the name originally meant 'he who fetched the distant one (fem.)'. From ḥrt 'heaven', phon. ḥry, ḥrw in ḥry 'above' and the related words. In two words for 'gate'  is derived from earlier signs for gateway, namely in rwty 'the double gate' and in ht, var. hyt, 'portal', whence the title smsw hyt 'elder of the portal'. There is perhaps a similar contamination in hꜢt 'ceiling'.

sign list.description: sky with a broken (?) was-scepter S 40 (?) suspended from it (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Det. night, exx. grḥ 'night'; wḫ 'night'; darkness, exx. kkw 'darkness'; ꜥḫḫw 'dusk'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: moisture falling from the sky (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. dew, rain, exx. idt, var. iꜢdt, abbrev. , 'dew'; šnyt 'rain-storm'.

Ideo. or det. in rꜥ 'sun', 'day'; hrw 'day';  in dates reads sw. Det. sun or actions of sun, exx. šw 'sun'; wbn 'rise'; day, exx. sf 'yesterday'; wrš 'spend all day'; time generally, exx. wnwt 'hour'; ꜥḥꜥw 'period'; (n)ḥḥ 'eternity'. For group-writing of  over  see N 23.
Ideo. or det. in rꜥ 'sun'.
Abbrev. for ẖrt-hrw 'day-time', 'course (of day)', lit. 'what belongs to the day'.
Det. (or ideo.) sunshine, exx. Ꜣḫw (Pyr. iꜢḫw) 'sunshine'; psḏ 'shine'; wbn 'rise'.  From this last, phon. wbn in wbnw 'wound'.  Phon. ḥnmmt in 'the sun-folk' of Heliopolis.

sign list.description: moon with its lower half obscured (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in psḏntyw, var. psdn, var. Pyr. pśḏtyw, 'New-moon festival'. Hence phon. det. psḏ in psḏt 'divine ennead', 'company of nine gods'. This sign is liable to confusion with the loaf  X 6.
Use as last.

sign list.description: Crescent moon (also vertically or vertically and reversed when used as det.)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in iꜥḥ 'moon'; hence phon. det. or abbrev. in wꜥḥ 'carob beans.' Combined with  N 14, ideo. in Ꜣbd 'month'; for the reading cf. an O.K. personal name Ꜣbdw and Sa`idic ebot 'month'; in dates abbreviated as  , ex. Ꜣbd 3 'month 3.' In abbrev. šsp 'palm' (as measure) the sign has doubtless a different pictorial origin. In some inscriptions  is written for  spr, F 42.
In iꜥḥ 'moon'.

sign list.description: combination of half of N 11 and N 14
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ...nt 'half-month festival'.

Ideo. or det. in sbꜢ, var. Pyr. śbꜢ, 'star'; hence phon. or phon. det. sbꜢ (śbꜢ), 'teach' (with derivatives); sbꜢ 'door'. Det. star, constellation, exx. Msḫtyw 'the Great Bear'; Spdt 'Sothis'; time as indicated by stars, exx. Ꜣbd 'month', see N 11; wnwt (1) 'hour', (2) 'priesthood'. Also semi-phon. dwꜢ, exx. dwꜢt 'morning'; dwꜢ 'adore' (in the morning). In the word 'netherworld' (originally the place of the morning twilight, popularly known as 'the Duat' and in this work still translated dwꜢt) the very common Pyr var. dꜢt probably indicates that the w had fallen and that the pronunciation already approximated to the Old Coptic te, tei.
Ideo. in d(w)Ꜣt 'netherworld', see N 14, at end.

sign list.description: flat alluvial land with grains of sand N 33 beneath it
sign list.notes: Ideo. in tꜢ 'earth', 'land'.  Hence phon. tꜢ (rare), ex, sštꜢ 'mystery', 'secret'.  In group-writing with  and  is t.  Det. land, in ḏt 'estate', whence also in ḏt 'eternity'; ḏt 'serf'.
Use as last.

Ideo. in iw 'island'. In group-writing with  and  is phon. i, ex. I͗rt 'Yareth' (Syrian place-name). Det. desert or foreign country, exx. Ꜣḫt 'horizon', more exactly the land of the sun-rise; Ṯḥnw 'Libya'; Stt 'Asia'; cf. too  D 8. Different signs, but with similar outline, are (1) the garment, see after S 26; (2) the cake, see after X 4; (3) the oval, see  Z 8.
In Ḥr-Ꜣḫti, 'Horus-of-the-horizon', 'Harakhti'.
Det. in wḏb 'sand-bank', 'shore'. Hence phon. wḏb in var. Pyr. wḏb 'turn back' and derivatives. From O.K. onward a sign of like appearance is used in ḥb-sd 'jubilee', 'Sed-festival'.

Det. land, especially in idb 'bank', 'region' (dual idbwy 'the two banks', i.e. 'Egypt').  More widely used in Dyn. XVIII, then often taking the place of earlier  N 23, exx. tꜢ 'earth'; Ꜣḥt 'fields'; dmi 'town'.

sign list.description: sandy tongue of land (O.K. prototype of both N 20 and N 21)
sign list.notes: In wḏb, see O.K. var. under N 20. det. land, exx. Dyn. III ꜥḥt 'field'; śḫt 'field'.

sign list.description: irrigation canal (Dyn. XI-XVIII; early identical with, and clearly a mere differentiation of, N 36)
sign list.notes: Det. irrigated land, exx. tꜢ 'land'; tꜢš 'boundary'; in Dyn XVIII N 23 tends to be replaced by  N 21. In Dyn. XI-XII  over  is found as det. of time, probably corrupted from  over two horizontal strokes as used in words for 'tomorrow' and 'yesterday', exx. tr 'season'; rk 'time'.

sign list.description: land marked out with irrigation runnels
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in sp(Ꜣ)t (śpꜢt) 'district', 'nome'; also in ḏꜢtt (?) 'estate'.  Det. province, exx. TꜢ-wr 'nome of Abydos'; Šmꜥw 'Upper Egypt'; also garden in ḥsp (Pyr. ḥzp) 'garden'.

sign list.description: sandy hill country over edge of green cultivation
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ḫꜢst (ḫꜢśt) 'hill country', 'foreign land'. Det. desert, exx. smt (zmt) 'desert', 'necropolis'; ḥrt 'upland tomb'; iꜢbtt 'east'; also foreign countries, ex. Rṯnw 'Retjnu', 'Syria'. Ideo. in ḤꜢ (the desert-god) Ha'.

sign list.description: sand-covered mountain over edge of green cultivation
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ḏw 'mountain', plur. ḏww.  Hence phon. ḏw (later dw), exx. ḏwi 'call'; Ꜣbḏw 'Abydos'; wnḏw 'short-horned cattle'.
Ideo. in Ꜣḫt 'horizon' (properly the place in the sky where the sun rises) and its derivatives.

sign list.description: hill over which are the rays of the rising sun
sign list.notes: Ideo. in Pyr. ḫꜥ 'hill of the sunrise' and in ḫꜥi 'appear in glory'.  Hence phon. ḫꜥ, ex. ḫꜥm, var. ẖꜥm, 'approach'.
Cf. qꜢꜢ 'hill', 'height'. Hence phon. q.
Ideo. or det. in iꜢt 'mound'.

Ideo. or det. in wꜢt 'road' and related words. Det. road, exx. mṯn 'road'; ḥrt 'road' (with related words); travel, in ꜥr 'mount up' and derivatives; position in general, exx. ꜥꜢ 'here'; r-sy 'entirely'; pfꜢ 'that'; distance, in ḥnty 'period'. Abbrev. ḥr (see ḥrt 'road' above) in I͗n-ḥrt '(the god) Onuris'; in ḥrw-r 'besides'; and for superstitious reasons in place of Ḥr 'Horus' on M.K. coffins; also abbrev. wꜢ in wꜢ r 'fall into' a bad state.
Phon. det. in Pyr. śinw 'runners' on account of sin 'clay'.  Also as alternative for  F 52 in O.K. mḥśḥś 'filthy one'.  In M.E. replaced by  Aa 2.

sign list.description: grain of sand, pellet, or like.  (For similar signs cf. D 12 and the circle, see after Z 8)
sign list.notes: Det, sand, in šꜥy 'sand'; metal or mineral (often repeated), exx. nbw 'gold'; msdmt 'black eye-paint', 'kohl'; medicaments, incense, etc. exx. ṯꜢ 'pellet'; pẖrt 'medicine', 'prescription'. A sign of like appearance rarely takes the place of dangerous signs such as  A 14 in religious documents, exx. ḫftyw 'enemies'; this practice dates from Pyr. Sometimes  is substituted for the plural strokes , exx. gnwt 'annals'; šsrw 'bags'.

sign list.description: ingot of metal (Dyn. XVIII; in Dyn. XI the sign resembles W 13; in Dyn. III-V it resembles X 3)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in 'copper', early perhaps read biꜢ and later ḥmt  (?).  Det. objects of copper or bronze, exx. ꜥnḫ 'mirror'; ḫꜥw 'weapons; minb 'axe'.

Cf. nt 'water'. Hence (?) phon. n. Perhaps phon. n too when used as a substitute for  D 35 both in n 'not' and nn 'not'. In ḏt 'serf'  replaces the sign of land  N 17, a curious substitution (or error of transcription?) found also in Pyr.

sign list.description: channel filled with water (later form as det. irrigated land N 23)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in mr 'canal', 'channel'. Hence phon. or phon. det. mr in var. mri 'love'; phon. mi, exx. mist 'liver'; miḥꜥt 'tomb'.  Det. rivers, lakes, seas, exx. WꜢḏ-wr 'the sea', lit. 'the great green'; ḥꜥpy, var. M.K. ḥp, 'the inundation', here early interchanging with  N 37.  For use with N (35) as det. of names of rivers, lakes, seas from Dyn. XVIII on, see under  N 35.  Doubtless an irrigation canal when prototype of the later land-sign  N 23, see there.  In the fem. collective mrt 'weavers' the sign  was probably understood as a weaver's reed, though the occasional presence of  or  may may have indicated the same value mr as in the masc. mr 'friend(s)', 'partisans'.

Ideo. in š'pool'. Hence phon. š. Not seldom interchanging in hieroglyphic with  N 36, ex. ḥꜥpyw 'inundations'. Appears to be a sign for irrigated land in śtꜢt 'aurora'; cf. the use of  N 36 both as a channel of the Nile and, in its use as the early form of N 23, as an irrigation canal. Sometimes  replaced the cake (see after X 4) in spellings of sn 'open'. Occasionally it serves as a large form of the block of stone  O 39, ex. inr 'stone'.

sign list.description: garden pool with sloping sides (detailed form of N 37)
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.description: garden pool full of water (alternative of N 37)
sign list.notes: Use as  N 37.
In šm 'go'.

Det. well, ex. ẖnmt 'well'; pool, marsh, in pḥww 'limits', 'distant marshlands'. As substitute for the female organ in ḥmt 'woman', 'wife'. Hence phon. ḥm , exx. ḥm 'assuredly'; nḥm 'rescue'. Also as female organ in 'vulva', and derivatively 'cow', where the reading is more probably idt than ḥmt; cf. above  F 45. For obscure reasons, phon. biꜢ, exx. biꜢ 'copper'; biꜢ 'firmament'; for the reading see biꜢw 'mine'.

sign list.description: well full of water (a common alternative form of last)
sign list.notes: Use as last.

Ideo. in pr 'house', cf. the fem. collective pryt 'houses'.  Hence phon. pr in pri 'go forth' and derivatives; only very rarely not initial pr, ex. for ḫpr 'become'.  Det. house, bulding, exx. ꜥt 'room', 'department'; iwnn 'sanctuary'; ẖnw 'interior'; mꜥḥꜥt 'tomb'.  Less suitably also in st 'seat', 'place'; nst 'seat' of office; Ꜣḫt 'horizon'.
In pr-ḥḏ 'treasury', lit. 'white house'.

sign list.description: combination of O 1, P 8, X 3, and W 22
sign list.notes: In prt-ḫrw  'invocation offerings'.
Ideo. in h 'room (?)'. Hence phon. h.
Det. in mrrt 'street'; hence phon. or phon. det. mr in Mr-wr  'Menvis-bull'.  For unknown reasons, phon. det. nm in nmi 'traverse'; also in nmi 'lowing' of cattle.

Ideo. in ḥwt 'castle', 'mansion', 'temple', 'tomb'. The full reading ḥwt, possibly later ḥyt, is suggested by the O.K. personal name Ḥwti and by the isolated variant Nbt-ḥyt, together with the Coptic equivalent of the name of the goddess Nephthys. Hence the transliteration ḥwt has been adoped in Gardiner's grammar except for the divine name Ḥt-ḥr 'Hathor', where the element ḥat is clearly in status constructus. However, in one passage of Dyn. XII it is used in ḥtt 'quarry', giving to  the mere value ḥ.
Use as last.
In ḥwt-ꜥꜢt 'temple', earlier 'castle', lit. 'great castle'.
In Nbt-ḥyt '(the goddess) Nephthys'.
In Ḥt-ḥr  '(the goddess) Hathor'.
Ideo. in ꜥḥ, var. M.K. iḥ, 'palace'.
In var. of ꜥḥ 'palace', see last.
Det. in sbḫt 'gateway' and in the related verb sbḫ (śbḫ) 'wall in', 'enclose'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: walled enclosure with buttresses, and with the signs W 10 and X 1
sign list.notes: Ideo. in wsḫt (wśḫt) 'hall' in palace or temple.
Ideo. or det. in tꜢ 'curtain(?)' and tꜢyt 'curtain'.  Hence semi-ideo. in the title of the vizier tꜢyty 'he of the curtain'. For tꜢ-wr 'larboard' see on  S 22.
Use as last.
Ideo. or det. in kꜢ(r)i (Pyr. kꜢr) 'chapel', 'shrine'.

Det. in Pr-wr 'Great House' name of the pre-dynastic national shrine of Upper Egypt at Hieraconpolis (Nḫn); also of itrt in itrt šmꜥ(yt) 'the row of Upper Egyptian sanctuaries', as seen at the Sed-festival; hence also as collective term for 'the gods of Upper Egypt'.

Det. sanctuary, exx. itrt 'row of sanctuaries'; ḫm 'shrine'; especially of the Pr-nw or Pr-nsr (Pr-nzr), names of the pre-dynastic national sanctuary of Lower Egypt at Buto (P). Hence itrt mḥt 'the row of Lower Egyptian sanctuaries' and collective term for 'the gods of Lower Egypt'; see on O 19.
Ideo. or det. in sḥ-nṯr (zḥ-nṯr) 'the divine booth'.

sign list.description: open booth supported by a pole
sign list.notes:
Ideo. or det. in sḥ, var. Pyr. zḥ, 'booth'; hence phon. sḥ (zḥ) in sḥ 'counsel'.  In the combination  the sign  retains a value ḥb (ḥꜢb) which it formerly possessed when used alone.
For  see W 4.
Ideo. or det. in ḥb-sd (ḥb-śd) 'jubilee', 'Sed-festival'.

sign list.description: pyramid with side of surrounding wall
sign list.notes: Det. in mr 'pyramid', 'tomb', and in names of specific royal pyramids, ex. QꜢ-nfr-I͗mnmḥꜢt 'the pyramid of Amenemhet-is-high-and-beautiful'.  Hence also in Mn-nfr 'Memphis'.
Ideo. or det. in tḫn 'obelisk'.
Ideo. or det. stela, exx. wḏ 'stela'; ꜥḥꜥw 'station', 'stela'.
Det. hall of columns, exx. ḏꜢdw 'hall of columns'; ḫꜢ 'office'.  From last, phon. or phon. det. ḫꜢ in ḫ(Ꜣ)w(y) 'night'.
Ideo. in iwn 'column'; for the reading cf. iwnyt 'hall of columns'.  Hence phon. iwn, exx. iwnt 'bow'; I͗wnw 'Heliopolis'.
Cf. ꜥꜢ 'column'. Hence phon. ꜥꜢ, exx. ꜥꜢ 'great'; ḥꜥꜢ 'infant'. In group-writing is phon. ꜥ, exx. Tꜥmṯ 'Taꜥmeti', f. personal name; Ynꜥm 'Yenoam', Palestinian place-name.
Ideo. or det. in sḫnt (zḫnt) 'support' of heaven.  For a similar sign, but reversed (with prongs down), see after U 12.
Ideo. or det. in ꜥꜢ 'door'; hence very rarely phon. ꜥꜢm ex, ꜥꜢmt 'Asiatic woman'. det. open, exx. wn 'open'; sn 'open'.
Det. door, gateway, exx. sbꜢ (śbꜢ) 'door'; sbḫt 'gateway'.
Det. in srḫ 'banner' for the Horus name.
Ideo. in s (z) 'bolt'. Hence phon. s (z). Also as substitute for  R 22 in Ḫm 'Letopolis', the modern Ausim, NW. of Cairo.

In a number of words implying motion and having s (z) as a characteristic radical, exx. sbi 'go', 'pass', 'send'; si 'perish', later replaced by sbi; ms 'bring', 'offer'; is 'go' (imperative); sy (zy) 'who?', 'what?'  There is much confusion in the value of , owing to the tendency (1) to write  alone for sb, and (2) to write for simple s.
Ideo. or det. in inb 'wall'.  Det. wall, exx. sbty 'surrounding wall'; wmtt 'bulwark', 'fortification'; snb 'overleap' a wall.
Det. overthrow, exx. shn 'overthrow'; sẖnn 'demolish' a wall; slanting, ex. gsꜢ 'tilt'.

Det. in qnbt 'corner', 'angle', whence qnbt 'magistrates', lit. perhaps 'those who sit at the corner'.  Det. gate, in ꜥrrt 'gate'; corner (?), in mrrt 'street'.  Ideo. or det. in ḥry (n) tm, an obscure title.

sign list.description: stone slab or brick (sometimes largle like N 37)
sign list.notes: Det. stone and similar, exx. inr 's'tone'; ꜥꜢt 'valuable stone' for vessels, etc.; dbn 'deben-weight'; ꜥr 'pebble'; ḏbt 'brick'.
Det. stairway, exx. rwd 'stairway'; ḫtyw 'terrace', 'terraced hill'.
Det. stairway, exx. qꜢy 'ascent', 'high place'; iꜥr 'ascend'.
Phon. šsp (šzp) in šsp, var. Pyr. šzp, 'receive', but early sšp; cf. sšp 'daylight'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: emblem erected outside the temple of Min
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in iꜢt 'office', 'rank'.
Ideo. or det. in ipt 'harem'; ipꜢt is possibly the fuller form of the same word.
Use as last.

sign list.description: a prehistoric building at Hieraconpolis (Dyn. XVIII form)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in Nḫn 'Hieraconpolis', i.e. Kom el-Ahmar in Upper Egypt.
Use as last.

Ideo. in niwt 'village'; for the reading cf. Pyr. n(iw)tyw (?) 'those belonging to the lower heaven'.  Det. village, town, ex. WꜢst 'Thebes'; inhabited region, in Kmt 'Egypt', lit. 'the black (land)'; ḏꜢtt(?) 'estate'.

Det. in spt (zpt) 'threshing-floor'.  hence phon. or phon. det. sp (zp) in sp 'time', 'occasion' and related words.  Note sp sn 'two times' as sign that a word or part of a word is to be repeated in reading, exx. ꜥšꜢ ꜥšꜢ 'very often'; ršrš 'rejoice'.

sign list.description: heap of grain on a raised mud floor
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in šnwt 'granary'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. boat, ship, exx. 𓂧𓊪𓏏𓊛 dpt 'ship'; 𓎛𓂝𓅱𓊛𓏥 ḥꜥw 'ships; 𓊢𓂝𓅱𓊛𓏥 ꜥḥꜥw 'ships'; sail, travel by water, exx. 𓈖𓂝𓊛 nꜥi'sail'; 𓐍𓂧𓊛ḫdi 'fare downstream'; also det. in 𓃛𓅱𓊛 iw(y) 'one wihtout a boat'. As abbrev. the sign presents difficulties; 𓊹𓊛 is doubtless dpt-nṯr 'the divine bark'; in 𓄓𓊛 'overseer of ships' there is definite evidence in favour of ꜥḥꜥw, but possibly ꜥḥꜥw is merely a later writing of, or more recent substitute for, ḥꜥw; the singular 𓊛'boat' doubtless usually stood for 𓇋𓐛𓅓𓅱𓊛imw, but once at least represents the much rarer 𓈎𓄿𓈎𓄿𓏲𓊛ḳꜣḳꜣw.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. in 𓊪𓈖𓂝𓊜 pnꜥ 'upset', 'overturn'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. in 𓏃𓈖𓏏𓊝 ḫnti 'sail upstream'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in 𓅱𓇋𓄿𓊞 var. 𓊞 wiꜣ 'sacred bark'. Det. divine boats, exx. 𓎙𓅓𓏏𓊞 mꜥnḏt 'bark of the dawn'; 𓈖𓈙𓅓𓏏𓊞 nšmt 'the neshmet-bark', i.e. the sacred boat of Abydus. Also det. sail, when divine journeys are meant, ex. 𓍑𓄿𓊞 ḏꜣi 'cross' sky, and said of Re.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Semi-ideo. in wḥꜥ 'fisherman', plur. wḥꜥw, together with the related words.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. ṯꜢw 'breath', 'wind'.  Det. wind, exx. mḥyt 'north wind'; ḏꜥw 'storm'; sail, in ḥtꜢw 'sail'.  Ideo. also in nfw 'skipper', late var. nfy.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Phon. ꜥḥꜥ in 𓂝𓊢𓂝𓂻 var. 𓊢𓂝𓂻 ꜥḥꜥ 'stand' and derivatives.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Use as last, ex 𓊣𓊛𓏥ꜥḥꜥw 'ships'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. oar, exx. wsrw 'oars'; ḥpt 'oar'. Perhaps from a word 'oar' known only from the king's name Nb-ḫrw(?)-Rꜥ 'Nebkherura' phon. ḫrw, exx. ḫrw 'voice'; ḫrwy 'enemy'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: In ḫr(y).fy 'says'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. in ḥmw 'steering oar'; ḥmy 'steersman'.

sign list.category_group: P, Ships and parts of ships
sign list.notes: Det. in mnit (minit) 'mooring post' and the related words. In hieratic often indistinguishable from  T 14 and consequently so usually transcribed.

Ideo. in st, var. Pyr. śt, 'seat', 'place'.  Hence phon. st (śt), exx. mꜢst 'lap'; nmst 'jar'; ws (wś) in Wsir 'Osiris'; Ꜣs (Ꜣś), in Ꜣst (Ꜣśt) 'Isis'.  From a word ḥtmt 'chair' (Dyn. XIX) phon. ḥtm, ex ḥtm 'perish'.
Ideo. in st 'seat' (rare).  Phon. ws (wś) in Wsir 'Osiris'.

Cf. p 'base' (for shrine), Ptolemaic p 'seat', Coptic poi 'bench'. Hence phon. p.
For  see M 7.
Det. in wsr (wśr) 'head-rest'.
Det. box, chest, exx. hn 'box'; ꜥfdt 'chest'.
Ideo. or det. in qrsw (qrśw) 'coffin'.  Det. in qrs 'bury'.

sign list.description: brazier with flame rising from it
sign list.notes: Det. fire, exx. ḫt 'fire'; sḏt 'flame'; heat, exx. rkḥ 'heat'; tꜢ 'hote'; cook, etc., exx. psi 'cook'; Ꜣbw 'brand'; torch, in tkꜢ 'torch', 'candle'.  Also abbrev. for srf (śrf) 'temperature'; nsrsr (nśrśr) in I͗w-nsrsr, a mythical locality.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ḫꜢwt, varr. ḫꜢt, 'table of offerings'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: table with conventionalized slices of bread
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ḫꜢy(t), varr. ḫꜢt, 'table of offerings'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: four-legged  table with loaves and libation vase
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in wḏḥw, var. Pyr. wdḥw, 'table of offerings'.  Also as abbrev., especially in the title sš wdḥw 'scribe of the offering-table'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ḥtp 'altar'.  Hence semi phon. ḥtp in ḥtp 'rest', 'be pleased' and derivatives.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: censer for fumigation (after O.K. doubtless misunderstood)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in kꜢp 'fumigate'. Hence phon. kꜢp 'harem', 'nursery', 'private apartments'; kp, ex. Kpny 'Byblos', a town in Phoenicia.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: bowl for incense with smoke rising from it
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in sntr 'incense'.  Also as equivalent of O.K.  W 10* in bꜢ 'soul'; also in bꜢ 'ram'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: cloth wound on a pole, emblem of divinity
sign list.notes: Ideo. in nṯr 'god'.  Hence phon. (semi-ideo.) nṯr, ex. ntry, var. Pyr. nṯr(i), 'divine'.  Very rarely det. for a god, ex. Gbb 'Geb'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in bd '(a kind of) natron'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: combination of R 8 and T 28 and N 29
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ẖr(t)-nṯr 'necropolis'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: column imitating a bundle of stalks tied together
sign list.notes: Ideo. in ḏd 'djed-column'. Hence phon. ḏd in var. Pyr. ḏdi 'be stable', 'enduring' and derivatives.  The twofold writing of the sign in the town-name  doubtless indicates the change of value from ḏd to dd.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Det. in iꜢt 'standard'. Also accompanyng various ideograms for gods, exx. Mnw '(the god) Min'; ḤꜢ '(the god) Ḥa. Cf. also  D 29;  E 18;  G 7;  G 26;  R 13.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: falcon G 5 on R 12 with feather (O.K. to Dn. XII)
sign list.notes: As emblem of the West, ideo in imnt 'west' and the related words. For the reading compare Pyr. imn 'right', 'right-hand'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: abbrev. of last, omitting falcon and enlarging feather (from Dyn. VI onward)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in imnt 'west' and related words, including wnmy, var. Pyr. wnmi, 'right' hand, side, etc.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: As emblem of the East, ideo. in iꜢbt 'east' and related words, ex. iꜢby, varr. Pyr. iꜢbi, 'left-hand'. From Dyn. XVIII on, by confusion with  U 23, phon. Ꜣb, exx. Ꜣbḏw 'Abydos'; Ꜣb.n 'has desired'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in wḫ 'the wḫ-fetish' of Cusae in Upper Egypt.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: wig, with fillet and plumes, on pole (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Fetish of Abydos, ideo. or det. in TꜢ-wr 'the nome of Abydos or This'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.description: the was scepter S 40 with fillet and feather
sign list.notes: As emblem of the Upper Egyptian nome of Hermonthis and its town, ideo. in WꜢst (WꜢśt), var. dyn. XX Ws(r), 'Thebes'.  For iꜢtt 'milk' see on S 40.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: As emblem of the goddess of writing ideo. in SšꜢt, var. Pyr. ŚšꜢt, late var. Sšt,  '(the goddess) Seshat'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: As emblem of the god of Panopolis (Ekhmim) and of Coptus (Qif) ideo. in Mnw '(the god) Min'. The name of Letopolis (Ausim) in the Delta reads Ḫm; from M.K. onwards  O 34 is often substituted for R 22 , see on O 34. Hence phon. ḫm in ḫm 'shrine'.

sign list.category_group: R, Temple furniture and sacred emblems
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.description: peasant's crook (N.B. not curved backward like S 38)
sign list.notes: Cf. ꜥwt, name of the sceptre of the shape .  Usually replaced in hieroglyphic writing by  S 38, but occasionally phon. ꜥwt, ex. ꜥwt 'flocks'.

sign list.description: sceptre with straight shaft and head of Seth-(?)animal (cf. too R 19)
sign list.notes:
Ideo. or det. in wꜢs, var. Pyr. wꜢś, 'was-sceptre'; hence phon. or phon. det. wꜢs (wꜢś), ex. wꜢsi 'decay'.  In hieroglyphic writing  usually represents also the djam-sceptre  S 41, exx. ḏꜥm 'djam-sceptre', whence phon. ḏꜥm in ḏꜥm 'fine gold'.  Phon. wꜢb (?) in WꜢb(wy) (?) 'the Oxyrhynchite nome', on the evidence of a twice found name of a locality WꜢbwt.  Phon. iꜢtt in iꜢtt 'milk', 'cream'.
For see R 19; for  see S 14*.

sign list.description: sceptre with spiral shaft and head of Seth(?)-animal
sign list.notes: Cf. ḏꜥm, name of a sceptre of the form .  Hence phon. ḏꜥm, occasionally in inscriptions of Dyn. XVIII in ḏꜥmw 'fine gold'.

sign list.description: sceptre of authority (it is impossible to distinguish separate forms for the various uses)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in ꜥbꜢ 'aba-sceptre'; hence phon. or phon. det. ꜥbꜢ, exx. ꜥbꜢ 'stela'; ꜥb(Ꜣ) 'shine'. From a sceptre named sḫm (śḫm), 'sekhem-sceptre', phon. sḫm (śḫm), exx. sḫm 'have power'; very late var. sḫm 'sisrum'. Ideo. or det. in ḫrp 'be at head', 'control' and related words, cf.  D 44. In title  is possibly always to be read ḫrp; at all events this reading is verifiable in some cases, exx. ḫrp nsty 'controller of the two seats', a priestly title; ḫrp kꜢt 'controller of works', cf. ḫrp kꜢt 'to undertake works', 'construction'.
Ideo. in md(w) 'walking-stick', 'staff'.  Hence phon. md in m(w)dw 'speak' and derivatives.
Ideo. or det. in Ꜣms (Ꜣmś) ames-sceptre'.

sign list.description: flagellum; perhaps originally used by goat-herds for collecting ladanum
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in nḫḫw, var. nḫꜢḫꜢ, 'flagellum'.

sign list.description: prehistoric mace with cup- or dish-shaped head
sign list.notes: Cf. mnw 'mace', name of this type of mace on M.K. coffins.  Hence phon. mnw, exx. m n.k 'take to thyself'; Swmnw, var. Smnw, 'Sumenu', a town where Sobek was worshipped, possibly El-Rizeiqat, 14 km. N. of Gebelen.

sign list.description: mace with pear-shaped head in act of smiting
sign list.notes: Det. in sqr (śqr), var. sq(r)i, 'smite'.
Ideo. in ḥḏ 'mace'.  Hence phon. ḥḏ, exx. ḥḏi 'damage; ḥḏ 'be bright', 'white'.

Det. in Ꜣqḥw 'axe'.

sign list.description: dagger of M.K. and later type

sign list.description: bow consisting of oryx horns joined by a wooden center-piece

Use as last.

sign list.description: composite bow with middle tied to bow-string when out of use
sign list.notes: Det. in Pyr. iwnt 'bow'.  From dyn. XII on preferred to  T 9 in the hieroglyphic writing of pḏt 'bow', 'foreign people', 'troop'; pḏty 'bowman', while  is preferred for phon. pḏ, pd.

det. in ꜥḥꜢ 'arrow'; šsr (šśr) 'arrow'; from the latter, phon. det. in sẖr 'overlay'. Doubtless from an obsolete zin, zwn 'arrow', phon. or phon. det. sin, swn (zin, zwn), exx. swn, var. Pyr. zin, 'perish'; swnt 'sale'; 'physician' swnw, var. O.K. zinw (?), the M.E. reading swnw on the evidence of a var. wr swnw 'chief of physicians'.

Ideo. or det. in rwd, varr. Pyr. rwḏ, 'string', 'bow-string'.  Hence phon. or phon. det. rwḏ, rwd, exx. rwd, var. Pyr. rwḏ, 'be hard', 'firm'; rwdt, var. rwḏt, 'sandstone'.  Ideographic det. in Ꜣr 'restrain'; hence phon. det. Ꜣr, Ꜣi, exx. mꜢi(r) 'wretched'; dꜢi(r), abbrev. dꜢr 'subdue'.

sign list.description: pieces of wood joined and lashed at the joint
sign list.notes: Semi-ideo. (?) in rs (rś) 'be wakeful', 'vigilant' and derivatives; phon. rs in rst 'foreign hordes'.

sign list.description: (1) throw-stick, (2) club as a foreign weapon of warfare
sign list.notes: (1) det. in ꜥmꜥꜢt 'throw-stick' with the related verb ꜥmꜥꜢ 'throw'; also in qmꜢ 'throw' and the kindred qmꜢ 'create', 'form' and derivatives. The combination in qmꜢ above-quoted and in ṯni 'distinquish' indicates that  is here the throw-stick, not the club, see on  G 41. (2) As club,  is found in Ṯḥnw 'Libya; ꜥꜢm 'Asiatic'. Extended gradually as det. to all foreign peoples and countries, exx. Tmḥi 'TemHi-land'; Nḥsy 'Nubian'. (3)  takes he place of various other signs, partly due to identity or close similarity in hieratic; thus it takes the place of (a)  Aa 26 in sbi 'rebel'; (b) of  M 3 in ḏꜥr 'search for'; (c) of  P 11 in m(i)ni 'moor'; (d) of  T 13, see under that sign; (e) probably also of  D 50 in mtr 'witness' and the like, though examples of such confusion in modern publications may sometimes be due to inexact copying.
Use as last.

For  see D 31.

Det. in snṯ (śnṯ) 'plan', 'plot out', 'found'.

sign list.notes: Ideo. or semi-ideo. or det. in šs, var. O.K. šś, 'cord', 'rope'. Hence phon. šs (šś), exx. šs 'alabaster'; išst 'what?'. There has been much confusion with 𓎤V33: (1) in the words 'linen', 'cloth', 'thing', 'concern' and 'corn', all originally reading śšr: however, the fact of the confusion, together with certain writings with metathesis šsr, make the usually accepted reading šs still just defensible, for final r usually falls; (2) as det. in ꜥrf 'tie up', 'pack'; (3) as phon. g in hieratic, where the two signs are not distinguished in early times; (4) as det. clothes, ex. isywt 'rags'; however, this employment to replace  𓋳S28 does not appear before Dyn. XIX.

Use as last.

sign list.notes: Det. in O.K. śk 'wipe'; hence phon. sk (śk), ex. ski 'perish'.  For unknown reason, phon. or phon. det. wꜢḥ, ex. wꜢḥ 'place', 'endure'.  Also det. in ḫsr, var. Pyr. ḫśr, 'ward-off'.  As corruption of a sign resembling  M1, det. in mꜥr 'fortunate'.

For  see O 9.

Ideo. or det. in sšr, var. O.K. śšr, var. Dyn. XVIII šsr, 'linen', 'cloth', cf. especially the compound sšr-nsw, var. O.K. śšr, 'thing', 'concern'; also in sšr 'corn'.  Perhaps through connection with the stem found in gꜢwt 'bundles' (see of V 32) or else with ggt 'kidney (?)' phon. g in a few words, exx. wgg 'misery'; Gbtyw 'Coptus', a town in Upper Egypt. XIX, and then mainly in the form  V 6 (see on that sign).  Note that in M.K. hieratic  is indistinguishable from  V 6; in hieroglyphic the two are very often confused.
Use as last.

XVIII 𓎛𓃀𓎱 ḥb 'feast'; hence semi-ideo. or phon. ḥb in 𓎛𓎱𓃀𓀜 ḥb 'mourn'.  Abbrev. of 𓎛𓃀𓏏𓎱𓍼ḥbt 'ritual book' in 𓎴 W5.  Det. feast, exx. 𓇷𓅂𓎱psḏntyw 'New Moon festival'; 𓍯𓎼𓎱WꜢg 'Wag-festival'.

Det. in wsḫ (wśḫ) 'cup'; hence phon. or phon. det. wsḫ (wśḫ), exx. wsḫ 'be wide'; wsḫt 'hall'; sḫw in sḫw 'width'.  Det. in ḥnt 'cup'; hence phon. ḥnt in ḥnwt 'mistress'.  Det. in ꜥ 'cup'.  In words reading biꜢ  sometimes replaces older  N 41, ex. biꜢw 'rare treasures'.

sign list.notes: Phon. nw, exx. nw (nyw) 'of', m. plur.; Nwt '(the goddess) Nut', probably so to be read (in spite of an obscure Pyr. var.) ḥnw 'vessel'. For preferred writing of initial nw see on U 19; final nw is sometimes written , exx. mnw 'monument'; Ṯḥnw 'Libya'.  Great difficulty is caused by 'primeval waters', which may have existed in two distince forms (1) niw or nww or nw, (2) nnw or nwnw.  Phon. also in (cf.  W 25) in ink 'I'.  Phon. det. in ḏꜢḏꜢt 'council'; whether the former writing has anything to do with ḏꜢḏꜢw 'pot' is doubtful.  So too from M.K. used in such words as qd 'build'; qd 'form'; the only phon. det.  here is due to the stem meaning of qdi 'go round', while the later  may be connected with qd 'fashion' pots.  From M.K. onwards inexplically accompanies  Aa 17, exx. nḏ 'protect'; nḏ 'ask'; and is found also in Nḫbt '(the goddess) Nekhbet'.  The writing for m-ẖnw 'in', lit. 'in the interior (of)' has been explained as a rebus m(w) ẖ(r) nw 'water under pot'.  Lastly, W24 occurs as occasional alternative to  or  as det. pot; hieratic often fails to distinguish these signs.

Use as last.  For  as the earliest form of N 34 see on that sign.

From this last, phon. det. sn (zn), exx. sni 'pass by'; Sni 'Senet', a fem. personal name; cf. also Pyr. iznii 'are opened'. In sni 'pass by' and snt 'likeness' X 4 is subsequently replaced by  X 5, while Pyr.  in zn 'open' later takes the form  N 37, see on that sign. Also from fqꜢ 'cake', phon. det. fqꜢ in fqꜢ 'reward'. As det. sometimes takes the place of  W 3 (Dyns. XI. XII), ex. ḥbw 'festivals'.

sign list.notes: Det. in pꜢt 'loaf'.  Hence phon. det. in pꜢt 'antiquity', 'primeval times' and the related words.  Apt to be confused with  N 9.

In. O.K. offerings-lists described as gśw 'half-loaves' or pḏw '(pieces) spread out'.  In Pyr.  doubled is ideo. or det. food, exx. wšb 'eat'; wnm 'eat'.  After O.K.  becomes indistinguishable from  N 29 and is practically confined to the word wnm 'eat'.  Exceptionally, however, as det. in snw 'food-offerings'.

sign list.notes: Ideo. give, in rdi 'give' and also in Pyr. for the more usual imperative imi 'give'.  The use in both stems seems conclusively for the ideographic character of the sign.  Possibly the earliest reading of the later stem rdi was rḏi, cf. the Pyr. var. for rḏw 'efflux'; but verb forms with repetition of the sign doubtless indicate the reading dd; so in Pyr. already.  From the same stem, phon. d (very rare), ex. dq(r) 'fruit'.  The word 'provisions' probably reads di; in hieratic the inner markings are not shown, see before Z 9, and the word has, therefore, often been read śpd.

sign list.description: papyrus rolled up, tied, and sealed (from Dyn. XII on also vertically)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in mḏꜢt 'papyrus-roll', 'book'. Hence phon. mḏꜢt in mḏꜢt '(sculptor's) chisel'. Det. writing and things written, exx. sš 'write'; m(w)dt 'word'; ḥqꜢ 'magic'; also abstract notions, exx. mꜢꜥt 'truth'; mꜢw(y) 'be new'; rḫ 'know'; ꜥꜢ 'great'. In mathematical books and accounts  is often abbrev. for dmd 'total'.

sign list.description: O.K. form of last (also vertically from Pyr. on in specific cases)

sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in mnhd 'scribe's outfit'; also in sšw 'writings' and the related words, cf. O.K. zš 'write'. Perhaps because pigments were ground fine and smooth, det. in nꜥꜥ 'smooth'; in the Ebers medical papyrus it is used as abbrev. for snꜥꜥ 'made smooth', 'ground fine'. Also det. of the Pyr. word ṯms 'red' with its later derivative tmsw 'injury', 'harm'.
Use as last.
For unknown reason, phon. mn, exx. mn 'remain'; I͗mn '(the god) Amun'; mnḥ 'wax'.
Ideo. or det. in ib(Ꜣ) 'draughtsman'.  Hence phon. ibꜢ in ibꜢ(w), 'dances'.
Det. in bnt (bint) 'harp'.
Ideo. or det. in sššt 'sistrum'. Between dyn. XIII-XVIII occasionally phon. sḫm (because of  sḫm, a kind of sistrum), ex. sḫm-ir(y).f 'potentate'.

Ideo. or det. one, unity, exx. wꜥ 'one', 7 'seven', lit. 'seven units'.  Following an ideogram  denotes that this means the actual thing that it depicts, exx. r 'mouth'; ḏw 'mountain'; so too in duals and plurals, exx. ꜥwy 'the two arms'; sbꜢw 'stars'; ḫꜢswt 'countries'; in fem. nouns the fem. ending t often intervenes, ex. ḥst 'water-jar'.  Such writings were often preceded in O.K. by phonetic signs; M.E. survivals of this practice are s 'man'; hrw 'day'.  Ideo. with  is occasionally followed by a det., ex. Rꜥ 'Ra'.  Misunderstanding of the function of  often leads to its displacement, exx. with s 'man'; š 'pool'.  Also with with a later writing of tꜢ 'earth'; dmi 'town' is likewise difficult to explain, as also are many later exx. of the stroke.  Already in Pyr. cases occur of ideo. with  being together transferred to a phonetic use; so often in M.E., exx. ḥr 'upon'; sꜢ 'son'; so particularly in group-writing, exx. r; ṯ.  Along similar lines with  as det. towns.  Occasionally in Dyn XII  serves merely to fill empty space.  In Pyr.  was sometimes used (like diagonal stroke and ) to replace human figures, these being regarded as magically dangerous; so in M.K. coffins, exx.  for  i 'O'; extensions of this use appear to be the rare employment of  as suffix 1st pers. sing. i 'I'; perhaps also the fairly common writing with  replacing  in s 'man.

sign list.description: stroke Z 1 thrice repeated (with various writings, vertical etc.)
sign list.notes:
Det. plurality, common from Dyn. IX onwards, following an ideo. or det. to show that it should be understood three times, exx. after  for rnpwt 'years' for O.K. ; also with nḏsw 'poor men'. Examples occur already in Pyr., but very rarely, ex. mrw 'canals'; these suggest as origin of the use a contraction of plurals like  into  plus , but since  are found as plur. det. from Dyn. VI onward (exx. wꜢwt 'roads', nḏsw 'poor men') the use of  as plur. det. cannot be dissociated entirely from the employment of , , or  in Pyr. as substitute for signs representing human figures which were regarded as magically dangerous; see on  Z 1;  Z 5;  N 33. In. M.E. Z 2 is found also with purely phonetic signs, exx. wrw 'great ones'; nfrw 'beautiful', m. plur.; nfrt 'beautiful', f. plur. Sometimes it marks plural meaning in words that are not themselves plural, exx. sn 'their'; ẖnyt 'sailors', a fem. collective; ꜥšꜢ 'many'; such plural meaning was probably felt by the Egyptians in words denoting foodstuffs, materials, etc., though singular in form, exx. t 'bread'; iwf 'flesh'; ḥḏ 'silver'; so too in fem. participles with neuter meaning, exx. ḏddt 'what was said', '(things) said'. Lastly,   is found with abstracts ending in w, whether these are really plurals or not, exx. šmsw 'following'; nḏsw 'poverty'; soo too with fem. infinitives, if such they be, ex. mswt 'birth'. For the same sign vertically written in hieratic, see under Z 3 (occurs also as phon. det. in ḫmt 'think').
For  see on N33.

Use as last, common in hieroglyphic from Dyn. XII, rarer in hieratic.
For  see on N 33.

sign list.description: two diagonal strokes (less often written straight)
sign list.notes: In Pyr. only as det. duality, exx. ṯn(i) 'you two' (cf. for the ending śni 'they two'); ꜥw(i), also ꜥw(y), 'the two arms'; and in O.K., ex. pḥw(i) 'end'. In some cases  replaced human figures, these being deemed to be magically dangerous, exx. Ꜣḫt(i) 'the two glorious ones' for sꜢt(i) 'son and daughter'; t(w)twi 'the two images'. The last use survives in M.E. Šdty 'Crocodilopolite', where, however, the hieratic  replaces, not dangerous singns, but signs difficult to draw; see below  Z 5. Elsewhere in M.E.  is always phon. y, through its constant association earlier with words of dual form, i.e. ending in i (y); exx. are .fy, var. Pyr. . fi, 'his two'; imnty 'western'; sḏmty.fy 'who will hear'. Except in compounds like the last  y is always final consonant; it has its distinct uses, and  is seldom interchangeable with it.

sign list.description: diagonal stroke as made in hieratic
sign list.notes: Identical in origin with stroke  being used in Pyr. as substitute for human figures, these being considered magically dangerous, ex. śmśw 'elder' with  replacing .  In M.E. hieratic used only to replace dets. that were difficult to draw, exx. Ꜣt 'moment' with  replacing .  In hieratic texts of dyn. XVIII sometimes in personal names without preceding phon. signs for  B 3, ex. I͗ꜥḥ-ms(w) 'Ahmose'.  Only very rarely to replace complicated or unusual signs in Dyn. XVIII hieroglyphic, ex. idt 'cow'.  Hieratic as substituted for two dets. (see on  Z 4) is merely a doubling of .

sign list.notes: Det. death, enemy, exx. m(w)t 'die'; ḫpt 'decease'; ḫft(y) 'enemy'.  In hieroglyphic barely distinguishable from  F 20.

The hieratic abbreviation of  G 43, best transcribed by , occurs with increasing frequency from Dyn. IX onwards.  In hieroglyphic  w does not become really common until the reign of Akhenaten.  Not to be confused with  V 1.
For  as hieroglyphic adaption of the more cursive hieratic form of  G 39, see on H 8.  For  as hieroglyphic equivalent of the hieratic forms of  T 13 and  U 39, see U 40.

Det. break, exx. ḥḏi 'damage'; gmgm 'break'; divide, exx. wpi 'divide'; psš 'divide'; ḫbi 'lessen', 'subtract'; actions involving something crossed or encountered, exx. ḏꜢi 'cross'; wšb 'answer'; Ꜣbḫ 'be united'; also in many words where the reason is not apparent, exx. nkt 'matter', 'trifle'; tꜢš 'boundary'; wdi 'emit (sound)'. Owing to its use as det. in certain stems,  has acquired special phon. or semi-phon. values as follows: (1) swꜢ, in swꜢi (śwꜢi) 'pass by', from swꜢ (zwꜢ) 'cut off'; (2) sḏ, in śḏt 'flame', from sḏi 'break'; (3) ḫbs, in ḫbsw 'ploughlands'; (4) šbn, in šbn 'mixed', 'various'; (5) wp, in wp st 'specify it', a phrase serving to introduce details of accounts; (6) wr (reason unknown), exx. sw(r)i 'drink'; ḫpr-wr, a medicament.
Use as last.

Cf. ḫ 'placenta (?)'. Hence (?) phon. ḫ.

Det. bodily growths or conditions, especially of a morbid kind, exx. wbnw 'wound'; ḫꜢyt 'disease'; wḫd 'suffer'; ẖpꜢ 'navel' (whence phon. ẖp(Ꜣ) in ḫpw 'sculptured reliefs'); fat, distended, exx. ḏdꜢ 'fat'; šfꜢ 'swell'. Replaces a number of O.K. signs that have become obsolete:--(1) = Pyr  V 38, as ideo. or det. in wt 'bandage'; wt 'embalmer'; sdwḫ 'treat', 'embalm'. (2)  =  Z 10, as det. in ḥsb 'reckon'; everywhere else  has survived as  Z 9. (3)  = Pyr  F 52 or O.K.  N 32, as det. excrement, in ḥs 'excrement'; smell, in sty 'odor'; clay, in sin 'clay'. (4)  = O.K.  W 6, as ideo. or det. in wḥꜢt 'cauldron'; hence phon. wḥꜢ in WḥꜢt 'Oasis'. (5)  =  W 7, as det. in mꜢt 'granite'; Ꜣbw 'Elephantine'. sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Pyr. ḥpt in phrase iṯi ḥpt 'take the ḥpt', i.e. 'proceed by boat', r a place; cf. M.K. ḏsr ḥpwt 'direct the ḥpwt' (plur.), i.e. 'sail'.  From M.K. there is a word ḥpt 'oar', but the writing in Pyr. makes it impossible to interpret that word as meaning 'oar' from the start.  Hence phon. ḥp, exx. Ḥpy 'Hepy', one of the four sons of Horus; ḥp 'Apis-bull'.  The full stem may have been ḥip, cf. Pyr. ḥip 'hasten'.
Det. in 𓏏𓌳𓐒 tmꜢ (from ṯmꜢ?) 'mat'. Hence (?) phon. det. ṯmꜢ in 𓍿𓌳𓐒 var. 𓍿𓌳𓎅𓈅 ṯmꜢ 'cadaster (?)' or kind of land (?).
Det. or phon. det. sqr (śqr) in 𓋴𓈎𓂋𓐓 varr. 𓋴𓐓𓌈, 𓐓, 𓋴𓈎𓂋𓌪𓂝 sqr (śqr) 'smite'.

Ideo. or det. in 𓍑𓏏𓏏𓐖 var. 𓐖𓏏𓏏ḏꜢtt 'estate' in the title 𓄓𓏤𓉐𓏤𓈖𓍑𓏏𓏏𓐖 'steward of estate'; the meaning of ḏꜢtt and the interpretation of 𓐖 here depends on the not improbable identification of this title with 𓅓𓂋𓉐𓏤𓈖𓈈𓏏𓏤 (var. 𓈙𓏏𓏤) in another tomb of Dyn. XII; the words 𓐖𓏏𓊖 'estate' would in this case read ḏꜢtt.  Hence phon. det. in Dyn. XVIII 𓍑𓍑𓏌𓏏𓐖𓀀𓏥 O.K. 𓍑𓆓𓈒𓏏𓀀𓀀𓀀 ḏꜢḏꜢt 'magistrates', 'assesors'.  For an unknown reason, phon. qn, exx. 𓐖𓈖𓏛 qn 'complete', 'be complete'; 𓐖𓈖𓎅 qn 'mat'.  In hieratic 𓐖 sometimes stands not only for itself but also for certain other signs, whence confusion have resulted both in modern transcriptions and in actual hieroglyphic texts. Thus 𓐖 is found for (1) 𓈈 N 24 in hierogl. 𓐖𓏏𓏤 spꜢt 'district'; (2) for 𓎙 V 26 in hieratic 𓐖𓆓𓈇𓏤 var. 𓐖𓈇 ꜥḏ 'desert edge'.  Possibly with some confusion with 𓊃 O 34, 𓐖𓏏𓈉 is found used in Dyn. XVIII hieroglyphic for smt 'desert', 'necropolis', as a mediating var. 𓋴𓏏𓅓𓐖𓏏𓈅𓏤𓈉 proves; for this reason the name of the Dyn. I king 𓍷𓐖𓏏𓏭 vꜥr. 𓍷𓐖𓏏𓏭𓈉 is possibly to be read Zmty rather than ḪꜢsty.
Det. in 𓐍𓅱𓂧𓐗 ḫwd 'rich'.
